clue.text: Composer's short cape

indicators.note: short means the composer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Sir Michael Tippett was an English composer

explanation.surface: A musician owns a cropped cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last T from TIPPETT; 'Composer's' looks like a possessive but just names the man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippet is a scarf-like shoulder covering worn as a small cloak.

clue.text: Polynesian artist outside a hospital

indicators.note: outside means the painter's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A Pacific islander painter waits beyond a clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps TITIAN round A + H; Gauguin, a famous painter of Tahiti, is the picture suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is an island of French Polynesia, so a native is a Polynesian.

clue.text: Strip, as do funny people who take off

indicators.note: funny signals the letters of Strip and as do are jumbled

explanation.surface: Comedians who mimic undress as performers do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like stripping, tying to 'Strip', but means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who imitate or mock others comically.

clue.text: Looking up offended god

indicators.note: Looking up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or offended

explanation.surface: An upset deity gazes skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'Looking up' reverses SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek deity of love.

clue.text: Statesman in Athens gets different replies about start of crisis

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round another here
different tells us to rearrange the letters of the word replies
start of means take the opening letter of the word crisis

explanation.surface: A Greek politician gives varied answers on a looming emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns REPLIES into PERILES, and 'about' wraps that round C, the 'start of crisis'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles was the leading political figure of fifth-century BC Athens.

clue.text: Say "Gee!" and lose your cool drink

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
Gee is the spoken name of the letter G
to flip is to lose one's temper

explanation.surface: Exclaim in surprise and lose your temper over a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee' looks like an exclamation but is how the letter G is spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot drink of beer or spirits mixed with beaten egg and sugar.

clue.text: One point on line for mathematician is excessive

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is a compass point, north
the ordinate is the vertical coordinate on a graph

explanation.surface: A single dot on a graph line goes too far for a maths expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, N; ORDINATE is the y-coordinate in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond reasonable limits; immoderate.

clue.text: Tongue that's all in gob? Not entirely

indicators.note: Not entirely means the answer lies inside the words all in gob, not using all of them

explanation.surface: A tongue is entirely in the mouth, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gob' is British slang for mouth, which makes 'Tongue' look physical; it means language.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a language or jargon.

clue.text: Austere English novelist

parts.note: stern means severe or austere

explanation.surface: A severe writer from England.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century writer of fiction.

clue.text: Jolly good speller

explanation.surface: A fine champion at spelling bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent, as dated British slang; and a magician who casts spells.

clue.text: Traumatic work for a farmer

explanation.surface: A farmer's labour is distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressing experiences are described as harrowing; also, breaking up soil with a harrow is a farming task.

clue.text: Rebound to avoid black cat

indicators.note: to avoid means a letter is left out of the word for rebound

parts.note: to rebound is to bounce back
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone springs back to dodge a black cat, superstitiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' removes B (black) from BOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big wild feline.

clue.text: Regular movement bound to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means we take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: bound as in tied up with rope

explanation.surface: A recurring motion is certain to make a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be heard' suggests 'sure to be audible', but 'bound' means TIED, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's rise and fall happens on a predictable schedule twice a day.

clue.text: New and old wine for firm

indicators.note: New signals that the letters of and old wine are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Fresh and aged vintages offered by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of the wine list, but it rearranges AND OLD WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed securely or settled definitively is firm.

clue.text: Oddly shaped item identified

indicators.note: Oddly means the letters of shaped item are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strangely formed object has been recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped' sounds like the anagram signal, but 'Oddly' is it and 'shaped item' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify with someone is to share their feelings, which is to empathise.

clue.text: Put on Medusa's snakes

indicators.note: snakes as a verb means wriggles about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S, all letters used

explanation.surface: Dress up in the Gorgon's serpent hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snakes' looks like Medusa's hair but is a verb telling us to scramble MEDUSAS; the S of the possessive counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected or feigned, as a manner or name one adopts falsely.

clue.text: Pictures youngsters keep at home?

indicators.note: keep means the young ones hold something inside them

parts.note: pups are young animals
in means at home

explanation.surface: Photos that children hang up at home?
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' is the containment signal; 'at home' is the standard crossword way of saying in.
explanation.definitionFit: Posters of attractive celebrities stuck on walls.

clue.text: Sovereign from Paris is knocked off a horse

indicators.note: knocked off means those letters are removed from the city's name

parts.note: taken as written
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A monarch from France is unseated from a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked off a horse' paints a fall from the saddle, but 'knocked off' acts on 'is', and 'horse' supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme, as a ruler with highest authority.

clue.text: Waterside setting — not Land's End, so to speak

indicators.note: setting means the letters are arranged afresh
not means a letter is excluded from the word waterside
End means the final letter of the word Land's

explanation.surface: A riverside spot, not Cornwall's Land's End, figuratively.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is a famous headland in Cornwall; here it means D. 'not' removes D from WATERSIDE, and 'setting' rearranges WATERSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedging phrase meaning in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Is king backing republic?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backing means the king's name is read in the other direction

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king

explanation.surface: A question of whether a monarch supports the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads like support for the state, but it reverses the king's name; Lear is the usual crossword king.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern country with an elected president, hence a republic.

clue.text: React aggressively as heroin is grabbed by yob

indicators.note: grabbed by means the lout surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a yob is a British slang term for a lout
taken as written
H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out when a thug snatches their drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbed by' is the containment signal; 'yob' is British slang for a thuggish young man.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike or speak violently against someone.

clue.text: Champ makes money, so we hear, alternately

indicators.note: so we hear means we use how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: champ means bite, and makes money means earns

explanation.surface: A sports winner earns a fortune, reportedly, taking turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' here is the verb to chew noisily, not a champion; BITE EARNS sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things one after the other in rotation.

clue.text: Storage unit in South African aircraft …

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a Boer is an Afrikaner South African
MB, megabyte, is a unit of computer storage

explanation.surface: A depot in a South African aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storage unit' suggests a shed or warehouse, but it is a computing measure; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A military plane designed to drop explosives.

clue.text: … aircraft dropping queen somewhere in the Hebrides

indicators.note: dropping means letters fall out of the planes' name

parts.note: Harriers are British jump-jets
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Planes drop a queen at a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 21; 'aircraft' is plural here, HARRIERS, and ER goes. Harris is part of Lewis and Harris in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris is the southern part of the largest island of the Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Still like peas in a pod?

explanation.surface: Even so, identical vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless or however; and identical, as peas sharing a pod look alike.

clue.text: Proposition girl after heading for London

indicators.note: after means the girl's name follows the letter
heading for means take the first letter of the word London

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl proposes heading off for London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for London' suggests travel but gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic and maths, a lemma is a subsidiary theorem used in a proof.

clue.text: Fail to mention some with hearts

indicators.note: hearts means the central letters of each of the words some and with

explanation.surface: Leave unsaid some card games involving hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' looks like the card suit but takes OM from 'some' and IT from 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out or not say it.

clue.text: Get away from fire, dropping temperature

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is removed from the gun verb

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: Escape the blaze as it cools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' is the verb to shoot, not flames.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperative to drive someone off, like a shout to scare animals.

clue.text: Right birds for twin brother

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: The correct birds for a sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus and Romulus were the twins said to have founded Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend he was Romulus's twin, suckled by a wolf.

clue.text: Old swan getting hot — river is welcoming situation

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: An elderly swan gets hot by the river, an inviting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swan' means PEN, a female swan; the Ouse is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A home or institution where all are made welcome is said to keep open house.

clue.text: Stop short after bear prepares for action

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word behind the synonym for bear

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate

indicators.note: short means the word stop loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Halt abruptly once a grizzly gets ready to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop short' looks like 'halt' but gives STO; 'bear' is the verb, giving STANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops ordered to take up battle positions are told to get ready for action in this way.

clue.text: German writer packing travel article with energy

indicators.note: packing means the first pieces hold another letter inside

parts.note: to travel is to go
the is the definite article
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An author from Germany fills a suitcase with a lively item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' suggests luggage for travel, but it signals containment; 'travel' gives a verb and 'article' the definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, author of Faust, is the great German poet.
